name: RCD-protected socket outlet
summary: Plan mark for a socket outlet with residual-current protection built into the accessory itself.
description: Some outlets include a residual-current device in the accessory so that protection is provided at the point of use. Plans show this by tagging the outlet with RCD or a small residual-current mark, letting the electrician select a protected accessory instead of relying on the distribution board.

This approach is used for single outdoor outlets, refurbishment work where the board cannot take additional RCDs, and outlets used for portable tools. The plan symbol should be read with the board schedule so the designer can avoid double protection or check discrimination between the outlet RCD and an upstream device.
The mark does not state the RCD type, rated residual current or test arrangement. A plain outlet on an RCD-protected circuit is protected at the board and is drawn without this tag.
readingNotes: Distinguish outlet-integral protection from protection at the board.
Look for the RCD type in the specification, not on the plan.
drawingChecklist: State rated residual operating current and RCD type.
Check discrimination with upstream residual-current devices.
Show the test button accessibility if mounted high.
distinction: An outlet on a circuit protected by a residual-current circuit breaker is drawn plainly; this form puts the RCD in the outlet.
